body:
PASS at 1021a2fa8e1d20ecdb1908a7256496f2bdd612c5

No blocking findings. The commit fixes exactly the one thing I blocked on, and nothing else moved.

The fix: P..R is one file, three lines added and one removed, in the mutation test only. The child now gets an explicit env built by destructuring NODE_TEST_CONTEXT out of process.env, which is the same idiom this file's neighbours use — attempt-workspace and two-fixture-activation both do it that way, and so do a dozen of the mutation suites. That removes the inheritance the finding named, so the mutant child reports on its own stdout rather than through the parent's test protocol.

Everything else is unchanged from the head I passed: B..R is the same six files as at P, with the test file going from +59 to +61 lines, and the gate, the contracts, the config and the scope test are byte-for-byte what they were. So the review I gave at P still applies to the parts that are not this test: the filter excludes a lineage receipt only when its attempt id is the review's own and its trusted role resolves to review, build/revise and unreadable receipts stay in and still refuse, legacy versions resolve through their trusted lane, untagged reviews filter against the full pool, and the author set is unchanged. The queue data is the same queue data: two config keys touched, three lanes paired with three contracts at 7/7, 13/13 and 9/9 paths, no path clashes, migration 0205 only in the currency card.

Out of the sandbox the card's exact command gives 82 of 82 pass, exit 0, with both SHU71_LINEAGE_OWN_ATTEMPT tests ok including the mutation that swaps the filter for "() => true" and asserts HOLD — so the mutation now both runs and pins what it is meant to pin. Codex's own run passed three of the five files and was blocked on the two that spawn node, which is its sandbox's EPERM rather than anything in this tree; it judged those from the code and reports no regression.

I am GPT (via Codex on the orchestrator box), reviewing independently.
